passages.text: The following discussion should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and the related notes included elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-K. We make statements in this Annual Report on Form 10-K that are forward-looking in nature. These include: ● Statements regarding our landfills, including capacity, duration, demand for and pricing of recyclables, estimated closure and post-closure liabilities, landfill alternatives and related capital expenditures, operating expenses, leachate and the ETLF event at the Chiquita Canyon Landfill; ● Discussion of competition, loss of contracts, price increases and additional exclusive and/or long-term collection service arrangements; ● Forecasts of cash flows necessary for operations and free cash flow to reduce leverage as well as our ability to draw on our credit facility and access the capital markets to refinance or expand; ● Statements regarding our ability to access capital resources or credit markets; ● Plans for, and the amount and sources of, certain capital expenditures for our existing and newly acquired properties and equipment and the funding thereof; ● Statements regarding fuel, oil and natural gas demand, prices, and price volatility; ● Assessments of regulatory developments and potential changes in environmental, health, safety and tax laws and regulations; and ● Other statements on a variety of topics such as inflation, impacts of trade policies or tariffs, general economic conditions, credit risk of customers, seasonality, labor/pension costs and labor union activity, employee retention costs, operational and safety risks, acquisitions and their contribution to the Company’s strategy, dividends, share repurchases, litigation developments and results, goodwill impairments, insurance costs and cybersecurity threats. These statements can be ‎identified by the use of forward-looking terminology such as “believes,” “expects,” “intends,” “may,” “might,” “will,” ‎‎“could,” “should” or “anticipates,” or the negative thereof or comparable terminology, or by discussions of strategy. Our ‎business and operations are subject to a variety of risks and uncertainties and, consequently, actual results may differ ‎materially from those projected by any forward-looking statements. Factors that could cause actual results to differ ‎from those projected include, but are not limited to, those listed under the heading “ITEM 1A. Risk Factors” and elsewhere in this Annual Report on Form 10-‎K. There may be additional risks of which we are not presently aware or that we currently believe are immaterial that ‎could have an adverse impact on our business. We make no commitment to revise or update any forward-looking ‎statements to reflect events or circumstances that may change, unless required under applicable securities laws. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: This Annual Report on Form 10-K and the documents incorporated herein by reference contain forward-looking statements based on expectations, estimates, and projections as of the date of this filing. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed in forward-looking statements. See Item 7 of Part II – “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations.” Risk Factors Related to Our Company and Industry Our industry is highly competitive and includes companies with lower prices, return expectations or other advantages, and governmental service providers, which could adversely affect our ability to compete and our operating results . Our industry is highly competitive and requires substantial labor and capital resources. Some of the markets in which we compete or will seek to compete are served by one or more large, national companies, as well as by regional and local companies of varying sizes and resources. Some of our competitors may be able to provide or be willing to bid their services at lower prices than we may be willing to offer, which could impact our ability to win new business or retain existing business, including municipal contracts that come up for renewal. We also compete with counties, provinces, municipalities and solid waste districts that maintain or could develop their own waste collection and disposal operations. These operators may have financial advantages over us because of their access to user fees and similar charges, tax revenues and tax-exempt financing. If we are not able to replace revenues from contracts lost within a reasonable time, our revenues could decline. In addition, existing and future competitors may develop or offer new services or technologies, new facilities or other competitive advantages. Our inability to compete effectively could hinder our growth or negatively impact our operating results. Price increases may not be adequate to offset the impact of increased costs, or may cause us to lose customers . We seek price increases necessary to offset increased costs, to improve operating margins and to obtain adequate returns on our deployed capital. Inflationary or other cost pressures may outpace price increases or drive the need for additional price increases; and contractual, general economic, competitive or market-specific conditions sometimes limit or delay our ability to raise prices or otherwise impact our plans with respect to implementing price increases. As a result of these factors, we may be unable to offset increases in costs, improve operating margins and obtain adequate investment returns through price increases. Price increases may also result in customer churn as we may lose volumes which we are unable to replace at equivalent levels, including from either losing customers to lower-priced competitors or new competitors entering our markets as we raise prices. credit_strengths.text: Revenue and operating cash flow have grown steadily across the three-year trend, with operating income rebounding sharply in the latest year. This scale and consistency underpin the issuer's ability to generate internal funds for capital spending, dividends and debt service, supporting a stable credit profile within the refuse systems industry.

Operating margin exceeds the sector median, reflecting pricing discipline and cost control in collection and disposal operations. Interest coverage also remains adequate, with operating income covering gross interest expense multiple times, providing a cushion against earnings volatility and supporting the issuer's investment-grade-like credit characteristics.

key_risks.text: The risk-factor passage highlights intense competition from national, regional and municipal providers, some with tax-exempt financing or lower return thresholds. Price increases may not offset cost inflation and could drive customer churn, pressuring volumes and margins. This competitive dynamic is a concrete earnings risk that could weaken cash flow generation and debt-servicing capacity over time.

Debt maturities are heavily weighted to later years, with a substantial portion due beyond the medium term. However, the current ratio sits well below the sector median, indicating limited near-term liquidity buffer. Refinancing concentration in later years exposes the issuer to interest rate and market access risk, particularly if credit conditions tighten.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow comfortably covers capital expenditures, leaving positive free cash flow that supports debt service. However, free cash flow to debt remains modest and below the sector median, indicating that internal cash generation alone may not rapidly deleverage. The issuer relies on consistent operating performance to meet its obligations.

Net leverage is above the sector median and sits just below a threshold that could trigger a weaker financial risk profile. With limited headroom, a small decline in EBITDA or increase in debt could push leverage higher. Interest coverage provides some offset, but the tight leverage position warrants close monitoring of earnings and debt levels.

overall_credit_view.text: The issuer exhibits a significant indicative financial risk profile, with leverage above the sector median and cash flow metrics that are adequate but not strong. The business benefits from scale and pricing power, yet competitive pressures and a tight leverage position limit financial flexibility. We view the credit as stable but sensitive to operational setbacks.

Shareholder distributions and acquisitions absorb most free cash flow, constraining deleveraging. While operating cash flow is growing, the combination of dividends, buybacks and acquisitions leaves little room for debt reduction. Our forward view assumes management prioritizes leverage management, but any deviation could pressure the credit profile.

credit_strengths.text: 於三年趨勢中，收入及營運現金流穩步增長，而營運收入於最近一年大幅反彈。此規模及一致性支撐發行人為資本開支、股息及償債產生內部資金的能力，支持其在廢物處理系統行業內維持穩定的信用狀況。
營運利潤率超過行業中位數，反映收集及處置業務的定價紀律及成本控制。利息覆蓋率亦保持充足，營運收入覆蓋總利息支出多倍，為盈利波動提供緩衝，並支持發行人類投資級的信用特徵。

key_risks.text: 風險因素章節強調來自全國、區域及市政供應商的激烈競爭，部分供應商享有免稅融資或較低的回報門檻。價格上漲可能無法抵銷成本通脹，並可能導致客戶流失，對業務量及利潤率構成壓力。此競爭動態為具體的盈利風險，可能隨時間削弱現金流產生及償債能力。
債務到期嚴重集中於較後年份，其中相當部分於中期之後到期。然而，流動比率遠低於行業中位數，顯示近期流動性緩衝有限。再融資集中於較後年份使發行人面臨利率及市場准入風險，尤其是若信用狀況收緊。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 營運現金流從容覆蓋資本開支，留下正自由現金流以支持償債。然而，自由現金流對債務比率仍然適度，且低於行業中位數，顯示僅靠內部現金產生可能無法快速去槓桿。發行人依賴持續的營運表現以履行其義務。
淨槓桿高於行業中位數，且僅略低於可能觸發較弱財務風險狀況的門檻。由於緩衝有限，EBITDA小幅下降或債務增加可能推高槓桿。利息覆蓋提供部分抵銷，但緊張的槓桿狀況值得密切監察盈利及債務水平。

overall_credit_view.text: 發行人呈現顯著的指示性財務風險狀況，槓桿高於行業中位數，現金流指標充足但不強勁。業務受益於規模及定價能力，然而競爭壓力及緊張的槓桿狀況限制財務靈活性。我們認為信用狀況穩定，但對營運挫折敏感。
股東分派及收購吸收大部分自由現金流，限制去槓桿。雖然營運現金流正在增長，但股息、回購及收購的組合留下甚少空間削減債務。我們的前瞻觀點假設管理層優先管理槓桿，但任何偏離可能對信用狀況構成壓力。
